overall: The AG found the Water Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law: no evidence of deliberation outside a meeting, and the October 23, 2013 notice topic was specific enough. Other claims were declined or outside jurisdiction. No remedy ordered.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged that a water rate increase, announced in a customer letter, must have been decided outside an open meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find no evidence that the Commission deliberated outside of an open meeting regarding the water rates.

allegations.summary: Whether the October 23 meeting notice topic 'Old Business: FY 14 Water Rates' was specific enough for the public to know the rate vote would occur.
allegations.key_passage: The topic listed on the October 23, 2013 meeting notice, "Old Business: FY 14 Water Rates," was sufficiently specific to notify the public that the Commission planned to continue to discuss the Fiscal Year 2014 water rates.

allegations.summary: Complaint named a public employee individually; the AG declined to review allegations against him because he is not a member of a public body.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore decline to review the allegations against him and only consider his actions to the extent they relate to the complaint against the Board.

allegations.summary: Complainant also alleged the water rate decision was made without a public hearing.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not govern a public body's requirements for holding a public hearing; therefore we do not review, and offer no opinion on, whether there was any violation of any public hearing law.
